UX surfaceBoot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

Surface3d

Surface3d — the exported scene handle: the engine state (scene, camera, renderer) plus the per-frame scalar state JS pushes through set_* calls (light, clear color, post amounts). Kept as one struct so the JS handle has exactly ONE drop point (destroy).

frame

ray_at

ray_at — screen-space picking ray: NDC pixel → world-space (origin, direction) — JS loops bodies with it (sphere tests per body, per-pick only).

inv_view is rebuilt from the camera's rotation + position — the view matrix's inverse IS the camera world transform (no general 4×4 inverse needed for a rigid transform).

  • @param sx @param sy Screen position in CSS px.
  • @param sw @param sh Canvas size in CSS px.
  • @returns [ox, oy, oz, dx, dy, dz] — origin + normalized dir.
  • @param {number} sx
  • @param {number} sy
  • @param {number} sw
  • @param {number} sh
  • @returns {Float32Array}

  • @param {number} node

mount

mount — bind a canvas to the page's SHARED GPUDevice and build the renderer around it. The device is acquired once in JS (getSharedGpuDevice) and passed to every artifact — per-widget devices exhausted the driver's device budget on a widget-heavy page (Windows/D3D12: create command queue failed with E_OUTOFMEMORY after ~100 devices). Sync: with the device in hand there is nothing to await, and a synchronous constructor can never leave a wasm-bindgen closure dangling (the async-future trap was the "closure invoked recursively" cascade). await on the JS side tolerates the non-promise return unchanged.

  • @param canvas The host canvas element.
  • @param device The shared GPUDevice (one per page, from the JS bridge).
  • @param w @param h Backing size in DEVICE pixels.
  • @returns The scene handle, or a JS error string on init failure.
  • @param {HTMLCanvasElement} canvas
  • @param {GPUDevice} device
  • @param {number} w
  • @param {number} h
  • @returns {Surface3d}
